title: Asbestos medical surveillance, recordkeeping and the competent person practice questions
description: 20 practice questions on asbestos medical surveillance, physician opinions, records and the competent person, from OSHA 29 CFR 1926.1101(m)-(o).

questions.question: A technician who is not a licensed physician will administer the pulmonary function testing in an asbestos medical surveillance program. What training does 1926.1101(m)(1)(ii)(B) require of that person?

options.A: A course in respirator fit testing given by the respirator manufacturer
options.B: A training course in spirometry sponsored by an appropriate academic or professional institution
options.C: The comprehensive supervisor course that meets EPA's Model Accreditation Plan
options.D: The same asbestos awareness training given to Class IV workers

questions.explanation: "Persons other than such licensed physicians who administer the pulmonary function testing required by this section shall complete a training course in spirometry sponsored by an appropriate academic or professional institution."

questions.question: A worker spends 45 minutes on a Class III operation on intact material, counting the entire removal operation including cleanup, and adheres fully to the standard's work practices. How does (m)(1)(i)(A) treat that day for the 30-day count?

options.A: It counts as a full day
options.B: It counts as half a day
options.C: It counts only if no exposure monitoring was done
options.D: It shall not be counted

questions.explanation: A day on which a worker "engages in Class II or Class III operations or a combination thereof on intact material for one hour or less (taking into account the entire time spent on the removal operation, including cleanup)" and adheres fully to the work practices "shall not be counted."

questions.question: For employees required by the standard to wear a negative pressure respirator, the employer must ensure they are physically able to perform the work and use the equipment. Under whose supervision is that determination made?

options.A: A physician
options.B: The competent person
options.C: The respirator manufacturer
options.D: The building owner

questions.explanation: Employers "shall ensure employees are physically able to perform the work and use the equipment. This determination shall be made under the supervision of a physician."

questions.question: Under (m)(2)(i)(A), at what point must medical examinations and consultations be made available to a covered employee who will work where negative-pressure respirators are worn?

options.A: Only after the employee's first full year of respirator use
options.B: Only when the employee reports symptoms
options.C: Prior to assignment of the employee to an area where negative-pressure respirators are worn
options.D: At the end of the project

questions.explanation: One schedule in (m)(2)(i) is "Prior to assignment of the employee to an area where negative-pressure respirators are worn".

questions.question: A covered employee reaches the thirtieth day of Class II work this year. Adequate records show that the employee was examined in accordance with paragraph (m) five months ago. What does the exception in (m)(2)(i)(E) state?

options.A: No medical examination is required of the employee
options.B: A medical examination must still be given within 10 working days, because the earlier one came before the thirtieth day
options.C: A medical examination is required unless the competent person signs a written waiver
options.D: Only the pulmonary function tests must be repeated

questions.explanation: The exception in (m)(2)(i)(E) reads: "No medical examination is required of any employee if adequate records show that the employee has been examined in accordance with this paragraph within the past 1-year period."

questions.question: The examining physician determines that an examination should be provided more frequently than the rule specifies. What must the employer do under (m)(2)(i)(D)?

options.A: Keep the annual schedule unless OSHA approves a change
options.B: Ask the competent person to set a new frequency
options.C: Provide such examinations to affected employees at the frequencies specified by the physician
options.D: Offer the extra examinations only if the employee pays

questions.explanation: If the physician so determines, "the employer shall provide such examinations to affected employees at the frequencies specified by the physician."

questions.question: Under (m)(2)(ii)(C), who decides whether the chest X-ray in the physical examination is administered?

options.A: The employer
options.B: The physician, at the physician's discretion
options.C: The competent person
options.D: The employee

questions.explanation: The physical examination includes a chest X-ray "to be administered at the discretion of the physician".

questions.question: Besides the history, questionnaire, physical examination and pulmonary function tests, what else must the medical examination include under (m)(2)(ii)(D)?

options.A: Only the tests listed in the employer's written safety program
options.B: Tests chosen by the employer's insurance carrier
options.C: Tests requested by the competent person
options.D: Any other examinations or tests deemed necessary by the examining physician

questions.explanation: The examination shall include "Any other examinations or tests deemed necessary by the examining physician."

questions.question: Which item does (m)(3) require the employer to provide to the examining physician?

options.A: The competent person's training certificate
options.B: The building owner's notification records
options.C: The employee's representative exposure level or anticipated exposure level
options.D: The objective data record for exempt products

questions.explanation: The employer "shall provide the following information to the examining physician", including "The employee's representative exposure level or anticipated exposure level".

questions.question: An examining physician prepares the written opinion for an employee in the asbestos medical surveillance program. Which statement about smoking must that written opinion include under (m)(4)(i)(D)?

options.A: A statement that the employee has agreed to stop smoking before returning to asbestos work
options.B: A statement that the employee has been informed by the physician of the increased risk of lung cancer attributable to the combined effect of smoking and asbestos exposure
options.C: A statement that the employer has enrolled the employee in a smoking cessation program
options.D: A statement that the employer will exclude smokers from Class I work

questions.explanation: The written opinion shall include "A statement that the employee has been informed by the physician of the increased risk of lung cancer attributable to the combined effect of smoking and asbestos exposure."

questions.question: What time does (m)(4)(iii) set for the employer to give the affected employee a copy of the physician's written opinion?

options.A: Within 90 days from its receipt
options.B: Within 6 months from its receipt
options.C: Within 1 year from its receipt
options.D: Within 30 days from its receipt

questions.explanation: The employer "shall provide a copy of the physician's written opinion to the affected employee within 30 days from its receipt."

questions.question: An employer relies on objective data to show a product cannot release fibers at or above the permissible exposure limit and/or excursion limit. How long must the employer maintain the record of that objective data?

options.A: For the duration of the employer's reliance upon such objective data
options.B: For one year after the project ends
options.C: For three years after the data were collected
options.D: Until the next OSHA inspection

questions.explanation: "The employer shall maintain this record for the duration of the employer's reliance upon such objective data."

questions.question: Under the note in (n)(2)(i), whose services may the employer utilize to maintain the records required by the section?

options.A: Only the building owner's
options.B: Only the examining physician's
options.C: Competent organizations such as industry trade associations and employee associations
options.D: Only the competent person's

questions.explanation: The note reads: "The employer may utilize the services of competent organizations such as industry trade associations and employee associations to maintain the records required by this section."

questions.question: Which of these must the medical surveillance record for each employee include under (n)(3)(ii)?

options.A: The employee's union membership status
options.B: Any employee medical complaints related to exposure to asbestos
options.C: The employee's payroll records from prior employers
options.D: The employee's driver's license number

questions.explanation: The record "shall include at least" items including "Any employee medical complaints related to exposure to asbestos".

questions.question: A building owner who communicated and received information on the identification, location and quantity of ACM and PACM sells the building. What does (n)(6) say about the written records of those notifications?

options.A: They may be discarded once the sale closes
options.B: They are sent to OSHA for safekeeping
options.C: They are kept by the abatement contractor
options.D: They shall be transferred to successive owners of such buildings/facilities

questions.explanation: The records "shall be maintained by the building owner for the duration of ownership and shall be transferred to successive owners of such buildings/facilities."

questions.question: On a Class II job, employees work inside an enclosure and use glove bags. Under (o)(3)(i)(E), what must the competent person ensure, by performing or supervising the duty?

options.A: That each employee has had a chest X-ray within the past month
options.B: That employees working within the enclosure and/or using glove bags wear respirators and protective clothing as required by paragraphs (h) and (i)
options.C: That the building owner approves each glove bag before it is used
options.D: That employees are rotated out of the enclosure to reduce each one's exposure

questions.explanation: On Class I or II worksites the competent person "shall perform or supervise the following duties, as applicable", including "Ensure that employees working within the enclosure and/or using glove bags wear respirators and protective clothing as required by paragraphs (h) and (i) of this section".

questions.question: On a Class III job, at what intervals does (o)(3) require the competent person's on-site inspections?

options.A: At intervals sufficient to assess whether conditions have changed, and at any reasonable time at employee request
options.B: Once a month, regardless of conditions
options.C: Only at project close-out
options.D: Only when an OSHA compliance officer is present

questions.explanation: "For Class II, III, and IV jobs, on-site inspections shall be made at intervals sufficient to assess whether conditions have changed, and at any reasonable time at employee request."

questions.question: Before Class II removal starts on an occupied office floor, the competent person has set up the regulated area and its containment. Under (o)(3)(i), what must the competent person also perform or supervise, as applicable, about people going in and out?

options.A: Lock the building's exterior doors for the duration of the job
options.B: Have building occupants sign a liability release
options.C: Schedule all entries for the night shift
options.D: Set up procedures to control entry to and exit from the enclosure and/or area

questions.explanation: On Class I or II worksites the competent person "shall perform or supervise the following duties, as applicable", including "Set up procedures to control entry to and exit from the enclosure and/or area".

questions.question: A supervisors' course used to train the competent person for Class I work covers abatement, installation, removal and handling. Under (o)(4)(i), which other subjects must that training include?

options.A: The contents of this standard and the identification of asbestos
options.B: Classification of chest X-rays
options.C: Administering pulmonary function tests
options.D: Writing the physician's written opinion

questions.explanation: For Class I and II work the competent person "shall be trained in all aspects of asbestos removal and handling, including: abatement, installation, removal and handling; the contents of this standard; the identification of asbestos; removal procedures, where appropriate; and other practices for reducing the hazard."

questions.question: Besides a course consistent with 40 CFR 763.92(a)(2) or its equivalent, how else does (o)(4)(ii) allow a competent person for Class III and IV work to be trained?

options.A: By completing a spirometry course
options.B: By reading the standard on their own
options.C: Pursuant to the Class I and II requirements of paragraph (o)(4)(i)
options.D: By 30 days of Class III work experience

questions.explanation: "Competent persons for Class III and IV work, may also be trained pursuant to the requirements of paragraph (o)(4)(i) of this section."
